summary: auth login --chrome --profile <name> (and auto-detection) could not resolve a Chrome profile whose directory was renamed away from the "Default"/"Profile N" convention, even though its cookies were genuinely present on disk.
reason: Confirmed live 2026-09-28 with a dedicated automation profile directory literally named "ConcurAutomation" (shown as "Person 1" in Chrome's own profile switcher) holding a real, cookie-bearing, logged-in concursolutions.com session: `auth login --chrome --profile "ConcurAutomation"` and the channel-qualified form `--profile "Chrome/ConcurAutomation"` both failed with `No Chrome profile has cookies for concursolutions.com`, and auto-detection (no --profile flag) never listed it as a candidate either -- so this was not --profile-specific. Root cause: chromeProfileDirNames() matched only a bare "Default" or a "Profile " prefix against the raw directory listing, silently excluding any custom-named profile directory from both resolveProfileByName and discoverChromeProfiles. Re-verified reproduced identically after upgrading past PR #2003/#2055 (mtime-stale binary ruled out as the cause) -- this is a distinct defect from both of those PRs, which touch the browser-automation-fallback mutation paths, not this one-time cookie-extraction step. Chrome's own "Local State" JSON file at the user-data-dir root (profile.info_cache keys) is the authoritative source for which profile directories actually exist regardless of naming, and was already being read manually as a live workaround this session before landing this patch to read it properly inside the CLI itself.

changes.description: chromeProfileDirNames() now reads "Local State" (profile.info_cache) for the authoritative list of profile directory names first, falling back to the original Default/Profile-N heuristic (renamed chromeProfileDirNamesFallback) only when Local State can't be read or parsed -- so behavior for installations the old heuristic already covered is unchanged. Also added chromeChannelDirsOverride, a package-level test seam (nil in production) so auth_test.go can substitute a temp directory instead of probing real OS-specific Chrome install locations; chromeChannelDirs() now delegates to it when set, otherwise to the renamed chromeChannelDirsReal().

New file (this area had zero prior test coverage). Covers: a custom-named profile directory is now discovered via Local State (TestChromeProfileDirNames_CustomNamedProfile); the original Default/Profile-N-only behavior is preserved when Local State is absent (TestChromeProfileDirNames_FallsBackWithoutLocalState); a malformed Local State falls back cleanly instead of returning zero profiles (TestChromeProfileDirNames_MalformedLocalStateFallsBack); and resolveProfileByName resolves a custom-named profile by both its directory name and its Chrome-displayed name (TestResolveProfileByName_CustomNamedProfile).

validated_outcome: go build, go vet ./..., and go test ./... (all packages, including the pre-existing suite) all clean. New tests pass; live-reproduced the original failure against the exact real-world profile that motivated this patch, then confirmed the fixed logic finds it by re-deriving the same Local State read manually via Python (pycookiecheat) before writing the Go fix, so the fix's approach was proven against the real file before being encoded.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: concur-pp-cli's README FAQ already recommends a separate tool, press-auth, as a more reliable cookie-capture alternative for exactly this class of problem ("a more reliable capture: press-auth login concursolutions.com ..."), and internal/cli/auth.go already has a tryPressAuth() integration point. A deeper fix might be steering users toward press-auth (which manages its own dedicated, always-fresh browser profile) rather than continuing to harden ad-hoc multi-profile Chrome detection.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: press-auth integration is a cross-CLI, Printing-Press-level pattern, not specific to concur-pp-cli -- better suited to a dedicated follow-up (or a /printing-press-retro discussion of whether generated CLIs should default to press-auth) than folded into this CLI-specific patch.
